### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

Tu es relecteur de code. Tu es en **lecture seule** : n'utilise `Bash` que pour lire
(`git diff`, `git log`, lancer les tests). Ne modifie, ne crée, ne commite aucun fichier.

## Méthode

1. Récupère le périmètre : `git diff --stat` d'abord (ou les fichiers fournis) et les
   critères d'acceptation du brief. Au-delà d'environ 400 lignes ou 15 fichiers, charge
   la skill `dev-team:large-diff-review`.

## Méthode

1. Récupère le périmètre : `git diff --stat` d'abord (ou les fichiers fournis) et les
   critères d'acceptation du brief. Au-delà d'environ 400 lignes ou 15 fichiers, charge

3. Si l'étape suit le TDD, vérifie que les tests écrits avant l'implémentation n'ont pas

   coller au code) : c'est un point bloquant.
4. Cherche dans cet ordre : conformité aux critères d'acceptation, correctness
   (cas limites, concurrence, erreurs), régressions, tests manquants, performance,
   lisibilité, conventions (`CLAUDE.md`, code voisin).

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

{"result":{"id":"e231a583-1c5f-4ff9-a96e-e154b092373d","assignees":[],"labels":["0d75b934-bc35-4b5d-9e3b-362237efc0a6"],"type_id":null,"created_at":"2026-11-15T12:48:10.923505Z","updated_at":"2026-11-15T16:38:55.107367Z","deleted_at":null,"point":null,"name":"P2-01 — Une seule saisie de cible : boutons « Run Diagnostics » et « Trace Path » dans le formulaire Diagnostics","description_html":"

Story

En tant que dev qui diagnostique un appel qui échoue, je veux saisir la cible une seule fois et choisir entre « Run Diagnostics » et « Trace Path », afin de ne plus retaper la même cible dans un autre onglet.

Critères d'acceptation

  • Étant donné le formulaire de Diagnostics, quand il s'affiche, alors il montre Target, Port, DNS Server et deux boutons Run Diagnostics et Trace Path ; ↑↓ passe des champs aux boutons (Rule 135).
  • Étant donné une cible valide, quand j'active Run Diagnostics, alors le comportement est identique à aujourd'hui (pipeline, résultats, enter explique) et aucun trace n'est lancé, ni pendant ni à la fin du pipeline.
  • Étant donné une cible valide, quand j'active Trace Path, alors un sous-niveau « Network › Path › <cible> » s'ouvre avec la table Hop / Step / Address / RTT du Path actuel (mêmes lignes locales, mêmes sauts, même issue) et le trace part ; l'activation du bouton est la seule action qui le lance.
  • Étant donné le sous-niveau trace ouvert, quand j'appuie sur esc pendant le trace, alors il est annulé ; quand j'appuie encore sur esc, alors je reviens au formulaire avec Target, Port et DNS Server conservés.
  • Étant donné une cible vide, invalide, de la forme host:port ou IPv6, quand j'active Trace Path, alors rien n'est émis, le champ est souligné et le footer affiche l'erreur au niveau Error (Rule 140), avec le même refus et le même texte qu'au Path aujourd'hui (D150).
  • Étant donné une plateforme non supportée (macOS, Windows, WSL1, DEVDESK-334), quand le formulaire s'affiche, alors Trace Path est grisé avec la raison dans le footer (Rule 130), l'activer n'émet rien et Run Diagnostics reste disponible.
  • Étant donné un Port ou un DNS Server saisi, quand je trace, alors le trace n'utilise que la cible et n'affiche ni port ni serveur DNS comme s'ils étaient pris en compte.

Hors périmètre

Retirer l'onglet Path (P2-02) ; refonte du footer du trace (P2-03) ; route lue une seule fois (P2-04) ; nouveau mode TCP ou diagnostic ; stage Path automatique dans le pipeline (interdit : le trace ne part jamais sans action explicite).

Hypothèses / Questions ouvertes

  • Hypothèse: le sous-niveau réutilise pathModel tel quel (audit, P2).
  • Hypothèse: l'onglet Path reste en place jusqu'à P2-02 ; pendant cette période il y a deux entrées vers le même trace. Livré seul, c'est un état intermédiaire acceptable.
  • Hypothèse: dans ce sous-niveau, le footer reste celui du Path actuel, la cible y étant affichée en lecture seule jusqu'à P2-03.
  • Hypothèse: Port rempli avec Trace Path : le trace s'exécute et un message d'information du footer dit que Port et DNS Server ne sont pas utilisés. À confirmer (alternative : refuser).
  • Questions ouvertes : le comportement ci-dessus pour Port/DNS Server (non bloquant).

Contexte

Effort : M — Audit : .claude/plans/net-view-ux-audit.md (proposition P2 ; checkout principal, non commité) — Décision : D150 point 5, docs/backlog.md — Brief : docs/product/network-map/brief.md

Refonte « P2 » de la vue réseau (4 onglets), décidée le 2026-11-15. Dépend de DEVDESK-335 (S-09) mergée. Ordre : P2-01, P2-02, P2-03, P2-04.

1	---
2	paths:
3	  - "internal/ui/**"
4	  - "internal/app/**"
5	---
6	
7	# TUI — Forms & Focus
8	
9	### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation
10	
11	- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
12	- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
13	- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)
14	
15	### Rule 104 : Modal window structure
16	
17	- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
18	- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
19	- Message in the center
20	- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
21	- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
22	- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)
23	
24	**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
25	the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
26	no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
27	background and the exact width of the frame.
28	
29	### Rule 113 : Form field spacing
30	
31	| Layout | Separator after the field |
32	|--------|--------------------------|
33	| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
34	| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
35	| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |
36	
37	`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.
38	
39	### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)
40	
41	**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**
42	
43	Obligations:
44	- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
45	- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content
46	
47	Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`
48	
49	Files:
50	- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
51	- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation
52	
53	**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
54	keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
55	documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
56	the user).
57	
58	### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering
59	
60	**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.
61	
62	| State | Prefix |
63	|------|---------|
64	| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
65	| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |
66	
67	`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.
68	
69	**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.
70	
71	**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.
72	
73	```go
74	// ✅ Single-line, focused
75	theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()
76	
77	// ✅ Multi-ligne
78	theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
79	theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()
80	
81	// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
82	theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
83	theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
84	```
85	
86	**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.
87	
88	**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.
89	
90	**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).
91	
92	**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.
93	
94	**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
95	the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
96	even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
97	callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.
98	
99	Forbidden:
100	- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
101	- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
102	- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
103	- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
104	- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form
105	
106	### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport
107	
108	**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**
109	
110	```go
111	// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
112	func (f *Form) View() string {
113	    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
114	        f.renderFields()
115	}
116	
117	// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
118	func (f *Form) View() string {
119	    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
120	}
121	
122	// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
123	func (f *Form) View() string {
124	    return f.renderFields()
125	}
126	```
127	
128	Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).
129	
130	### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)
131	
132	**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**
133	
134	It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
135	an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
136	application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
137	a different thing from an exclusive choice.
138	
139	#### Visual
140	
141	```
142	  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
143	● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
144	```
145	
146	Line structure:
147	
148	| Part | Value |
149	|--------|--------|
150	| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
151	| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
152	| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
153	| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
154	| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |
155	
156	#### Navigation
157	
158	- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
159	- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field
160	
161	Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.
162	
163	#### Reference implementation
164	
165	```go
166	// Rendu
167	func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
168	    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
169	    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
170	    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
171	        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
172	    }
173	    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
174	}
175	
176	// Key handling
177	case "left":
178	    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
179	        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
180	    }
181	case "right":
182	    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
183	        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
184	    }
185	```
186	
187	Forbidden:
188	- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
189	- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
190	- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
191	- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)
192	
193	### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses
194	
195	Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:
196	
197	| State | Icon |
198	|------|-------|
199	| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
200	| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
201	| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |
202	
203	Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
204	Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).
205	
206	**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
207	column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
208	`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
209	`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
210	Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
211	the three icons above, unchanged.
212	
213	### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory
214	
215	**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).
216	
217	Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.
218	
219	#### API
220	
221	```go
222	// Creation
223	field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")
224	
225	// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
226	field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)
227	
228	// Focus / Blur
229	field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
230	field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()
231	
232	// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
233	field, cmd = field.Update(msg)
234	
235	// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
236	return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()
237	
238	// Retrieving the value on submit
239	value := field.Value()
240	```
241	
242	#### `wrapWidth` parameter
243	
244	`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).
245	
246	| Context | Recommended value |
247	|----------|--------------------|
248	| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
249	| Short notes field | `60` |
250	| Long text field | `100` |
251	
252	```go
253	// ✅ CORRECT
254	const descWrapWidth = 80
255	descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")
256	
257	// ❌ WRONG
258	descInput := textarea.New()
259	```
260	
261	#### Behavior
262	
263	- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
264	- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
265	- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
266	- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position
267	
268	Forbidden:
269	- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
270	- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
271	- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler
272	
273	### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️
274	
275	**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.
276	
277	| Key | Exclusive role |
278	|--------|---------------|
279	| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
280	| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
281	| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
282	| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
283	| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
284	| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |
285	
286	**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
287	suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
288	command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.
289	
290	#### Detailed rules
291	
292	**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
293	- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
294	- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
295	- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)
296	
297	**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
298	- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
299	- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)
300	
301	**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
302	- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
303	- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal
304	- Reference implementation: `LaunchForm` (`internal/ui/oci_resources`), pinned by `launch_form_keys_test.go` — `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox`, `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`, `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox`
305	- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it
306	- **Confirmation buttons are the mirror case**: `Space` never answers Yes or No. `components.ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal`, `OptionConfirmModal` and the setup wizard's confirmation answer on `enter` only (plus `y`/`n` on the yes/no ones). In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored
307	
308	**`Enter` — validation / action**
309	- Validates the currently focused button
310	- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
311	- Must **not** toggle a checkbox
312	
313	**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
314	- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
315	- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
316	- Must **not** move focus between form fields
317	
318	#### Common violations to avoid
319	
320	```go
321	// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
322	case "tab":
323	    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount
324	
325	// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
326	case "enter":
327	    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
328	        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
329	    }
330	
331	// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
332	case keymap.Space:
333	    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
334	        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
335	    }
336	
337	// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
338	case "up":
339	    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
340	case "down":
341	    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
342	```
343	
344	### Rule 140 : An invalid field is underlined, and the footer says why (DEVDESK-292)
345	
346	**A field that fails validation gets a wavy red underline, and the same error is in the footer. The underline is never the only carrier.**
347	
348	- **One entry point.** The underline comes from `theme.StyleInvalidField(base)` (curly underline, `UnderlineCurly`, colour `theme.ColorInvalidField`). Never call `Underline*` anywhere else: `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint` fails the suite. For a `textinput` use `theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&ti, invalid)`; for a `WrappedInput`, `SetInvalid(bool)`.
349	- **Colour.** `theme.ColorInvalidField` is a closed alias of `ColorFooterError` (no theme key, Rule 119). Its contrast against `ColorBackground` is at least 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), tested on every shipped theme.
350	- **The message is in the footer, level Error (Rule 128)**, taken from `components.Validation.Status()`. It is derived on every render, so it does not vanish after 3 s like a timed `footer.Error()`. The parent view returns it from its status function while the form is open.
351	- **Nothing is invalid before the first refused submit.** After it, every change revalidates the whole form (`Validation.Revalidate`) and the footer follows.
352	- **A required field left empty:** its placeholder is underlined. A focused empty `WrappedInput` shows a cursor, not its placeholder: nothing to underline, the footer carries the message.
353	- **Spaces are not underlined** (`UnderlineSpaces(false)`), otherwise the `textinput` padding would be underlined across the whole width. A value made only of spaces is therefore not underlined: the footer is the only carrier.
354	- **Restyle on a change of state only.** `SetTextInputInvalid` resets the cursor blink (`IsBlinked` goes back to false), so calling it on every message freezes the cursor. Go through `components.InvalidMarks.Sync(key, &ti, invalid)`, from `Update()` only (Rule 110), never from `View()` or a `Cmd`.
355	- **Prefix unchanged.** The focus prefix `●` stays as in Rule 120. The underline adds no cell: the rendered width does not change.
356	- **Fallback.** A terminal without styled underlines gets a plain underline (SGR 4), still readable. Cost: about 60 bytes per underlined character. Risk: SGR 58 and `4:3` on old terminals, to check by hand.
357	
358	```go
359	// ✅ CORRECT — state change only, in Update()
360	f.validation.Revalidate(f.errors())
361	f.marks.Sync(keyName, &f.nameInput, f.validation.Invalid(keyName))
362	
363	// ❌ WRONG — a local underline, and a restyle on every message
364	f.nameInput.SetStyles(lipgloss.NewStyle().Underline(true)...)
365	theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&f.nameInput, true) // in every Update
366	```
367	
368	Forms covered, and where the rules live: `docs/architecture/ui-components.md` ("Invalid form fields"). Out of scope: `templates/form.go`, netdiag, the `ctrl+p` palette, `FilterBar`.
369	
370	Guards: `internal/ui/theme/source_guard_test.go` (`TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo`, `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint`, `TestGuardDetectors`).

---
paths:
  - "internal/ui/**"
  - "internal/app/**"
---

# TUI — Forms & Focus

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

#### Detailed rules

**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal
- Reference implementation: `LaunchForm` (`internal/ui/oci_resources`), pinned by `launch_form_keys_test.go` — `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox`, `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`, `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox`
- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it
- **Confirmation buttons are the mirror case**: `Space` never answers Yes or No. `components.ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal`, `OptionConfirmModal` and the setup wizard's confirmation answer on `enter` only (plus `y`/`n` on the yes/no ones). In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored

**`Enter` — validation / action**
- Validates the currently focused button
- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
- Must **not** toggle a checkbox

**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
- Must **not** move focus between form fields

#### Common violations to avoid

```go
// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
case "tab":
    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount

// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
case "enter":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
case keymap.Space:
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
case "up":
    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
case "down":
    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
```

### Rule 140 : An invalid field is underlined, and the footer says why (DEVDESK-292)

**A field that fails validation gets a wavy red underline, and the same error is in the footer. The underline is never the only carrier.**

- **One entry point.** The underline comes from `theme.StyleInvalidField(base)` (curly underline, `UnderlineCurly`, colour `theme.ColorInvalidField`). Never call `Underline*` anywhere else: `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint` fails the suite. For a `textinput` use `theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&ti, invalid)`; for a `WrappedInput`, `SetInvalid(bool)`.
- **Colour.** `theme.ColorInvalidField` is a closed alias of `ColorFooterError` (no theme key, Rule 119). Its contrast against `ColorBackground` is at least 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), tested on every shipped theme.
- **The message is in the footer, level Error (Rule 128)**, taken from `components.Validation.Status()`. It is derived on every render, so it does not vanish after 3 s like a timed `footer.Error()`. The parent view returns it from its status function while the form is open.
- **Nothing is invalid before the first refused submit.** After it, every change revalidates the whole form (`Validation.Revalidate`) and the footer follows.
- **A required field left empty:** its placeholder is underlined. A focused empty `WrappedInput` shows a cursor, not its placeholder: nothing to underline, the footer carries the message.
- **Spaces are not underlined** (`UnderlineSpaces(false)`), otherwise the `textinput` padding would be underlined across the whole width. A value made only of spaces is therefore not underlined: the footer is the only carrier.
- **Restyle on a change of state only.** `SetTextInputInvalid` resets the cursor blink (`IsBlinked` goes back to false), so calling it on every message freezes the cursor. Go through `components.InvalidMarks.Sync(key, &ti, invalid)`, from `Update()` only (Rule 110), never from `View()` or a `Cmd`.
- **Prefix unchanged.** The focus prefix `●` stays as in Rule 120. The underline adds no cell: the rendered width does not change.
- **Fallback.** A terminal without styled underlines gets a plain underline (SGR 4), still readable. Cost: about 60 bytes per underlined character. Risk: SGR 58 and `4:3` on old terminals, to check by hand.

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — state change only, in Update()
f.validation.Revalidate(f.errors())
f.marks.Sync(keyName, &f.nameInput, f.validation.Invalid(keyName))

// ❌ WRONG — a local underline, and a restyle on every message
f.nameInput.SetStyles(lipgloss.NewStyle().Underline(true)...)
theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&f.nameInput, true) // in every Update
```

Forms covered, and where the rules live: `docs/architecture/ui-components.md` ("Invalid form fields"). Out of scope: `templates/form.go`, netdiag, the `ctrl+p` palette, `FilterBar`.

Guards: `internal/ui/theme/source_guard_test.go` (`TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo`, `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint`, `TestGuardDetectors`).

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a Path tab (native path trace, native Linux and WSL2 only: on macOS, Windows and WSL1 `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row prefills it; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target field refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR`, Linux only) |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)

- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.

  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

7	# TUI — Forms & Focus

10
