12	- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
13	- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)
14	
15	### Rule 104 : Modal window structure
16	
17	- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
18	- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
19	- Message in the center
20	- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
21	- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
22	- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)
23	
24	**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
25	the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
26	no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
27	background and the exact width of the frame.
28	
29	### Rule 113 : Form field spacing
30	
31	| Layout | Separator after the field |
32	|--------|--------------------------|
33	| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
34	| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
35	| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |
36	
37	`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.
38	
39	### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)
40	
41	**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**
42	
43	Obligations:
44	- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
45	- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content
46	
47	Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`
48	
49	Files:
50	- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
51	- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation
52	
53	**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
54	keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
55	documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
56	the user).
57	
58	### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering
59	
60	**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.
61	
62	| State | Prefix |
63	|------|---------|
64	| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
65	| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |
66	
67	`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.
68	
69	**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.
70	
71	**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.
72	
73	```go
74	// ✅ Single-line, focused
75	theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()
76	
77	// ✅ Multi-ligne
78	theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
79	theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()
80	
81	// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
82	theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
83	theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
84	```
85	
86	**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.
87	
88	**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.
89	
90	**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).
91	
92	**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.
93	
94	**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
95	the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
96	even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
97	callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.
98	
99	Forbidden:
100	- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
101	- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
102	- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
103	- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
104	- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form
105	
106	### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport
107	
108	**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**
109	
110	```go
111	// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
112	func (f *Form) View() string {
113	    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
114	        f.renderFields()
115	}
116	
117	// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
118	func (f *Form) View() string {
119	    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
120	}
121	
122	// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
123	func (f *Form) View() string {
124	    return f.renderFields()
125	}
126	```
127	
128	Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).
129	
130	### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)
131	
132	**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**
133	
134	It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
135	an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
136	application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
137	a different thing from an exclusive choice.
138	
139	#### Visual
140	
141	```
142	  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
143	● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
144	```
145	
146	Line structure:
147	
148	| Part | Value |
149	|--------|--------|
150	| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
151	| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
152	| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
153	| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
154	| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |
155	
156	#### Navigation
157	
158	- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
159	- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field
160	
161	Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.
162	
163	#### Reference implementation
164	
165	```go
166	// Rendu
167	func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
168	    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
169	    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
170	    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
171	        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
172	    }
173	    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
174	}
175	
176	// Key handling
177	case "left":
178	    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
179	        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
180	    }
181	case "right":
182	    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
183	        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
184	    }
185	```
186	
187	Forbidden:
188	- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
189	- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
190	- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
191	- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)
192	
193	### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses
194	
195	Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:
196	
197	| State | Icon |
198	|------|-------|
199	| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
200	| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
201	| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |
202	
203	Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
204	Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).
205	
206	**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
207	column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
208	`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
209	`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
210	Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
211	the three icons above, unchanged.
212	
213	### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory
214	
215	**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).
216	
217	Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.
218	
219	#### API
220	
221	```go
222	// Creation
223	field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")
224	
225	// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
226	field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)
227	
228	// Focus / Blur
229	field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
230	field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()
231	
232	// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
233	field, cmd = field.Update(msg)
234	
235	// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
236	return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()
237	
238	// Retrieving the value on submit
239	value := field.Value()
240	```
241	
242	#### `wrapWidth` parameter
243	
244	`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).
245	
246	| Context | Recommended value |
247	|----------|--------------------|
248	| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
249	| Short notes field | `60` |
250	| Long text field | `100` |
251	
252	```go
253	// ✅ CORRECT
254	const descWrapWidth = 80
255	descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")
256	
257	// ❌ WRONG
258	descInput := textarea.New()
259	```
260	
261	#### Behavior
262	
263	- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
264	- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
265	- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
266	- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position
267	
268	Forbidden:
269	- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
270	- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
271	- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler
272	
273	### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️
274	
275	**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.
276	
277	| Key | Exclusive role |
278	|--------|---------------|
279	| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
280	| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
281	| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
282	| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
283	| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
284	| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |
285	
286	**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
287	suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
288	command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.
289	
290	#### Detailed rules
291	
292	**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
293	- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
294	- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
295	- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)
296	
297	**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
298	- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
299	- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)
300	
301	**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
302	- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
303	- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal
304	- Reference implementation: `LaunchForm` (`internal/ui/oci_resources`), pinned by `launch_form_keys_test.go` — `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox`, `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`, `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox`
305	- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it
306	- **Confirmation buttons are the mirror case**: `Space` never answers Yes or No. `components.ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal`, `OptionConfirmModal` and the setup wizard's confirmation answer on `enter` only (plus `y`/`n` on the yes/no ones). In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored
307	
308	**`Enter` — validation / action**
309	- Validates the currently focused button
310	- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
311	- Must **not** toggle a checkbox
312	
313	**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
314	- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
315	- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
316	- Must **not** move focus between form fields
317	
318	#### Common violations to avoid
319	
320	```go
321	// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
322	case "tab":
323	    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount
324	
325	// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
326	case "enter":
327	    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
328	        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
329	    }
330	
331	// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
332	case keymap.Space:
333	    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
334	        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
335	    }
336	
337	// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
338	case "up":
339	    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
340	case "down":
341	    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
342	```
343	
344	### Rule 140 : An invalid field is underlined, and the footer says why (DEVDESK-292)
345	
346	**A field that fails validation gets a wavy red underline, and the same error is in the footer. The underline is never the only carrier.**
347	
348	- **One entry point.** The underline comes from `theme.StyleInvalidField(base)` (curly underline, `UnderlineCurly`, colour `theme.ColorInvalidField`). Never call `Underline*` anywhere else: `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint` fails the suite. For a `textinput` use `theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&ti, invalid)`; for a `WrappedInput`, `SetInvalid(bool)`.
349	- **Colour.** `theme.ColorInvalidField` is a closed alias of `ColorFooterError` (no theme key, Rule 119). Its contrast against `ColorBackground` is at least 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11), tested on every shipped theme.
350	- **The message is in the footer, level Error (Rule 128)**, taken from `components.Validation.Status()`. It is derived on every render, so it does not vanish after 3 s like a timed `footer.Error()`. The parent view returns it from its status function while the form is open.
351	- **Nothing is invalid before the first refused submit.** After it, every change revalidates the whole form (`Validation.Revalidate`) and the footer follows.
352	- **A required field left empty:** its placeholder is underlined. A focused empty `WrappedInput` shows a cursor, not its placeholder: nothing to underline, the footer carries the message.
353	- **Spaces are not underlined** (`UnderlineSpaces(false)`), otherwise the `textinput` padding would be underlined across the whole width. A value made only of spaces is therefore not underlined: the footer is the only carrier.
354	- **Restyle on a change of state only.** `SetTextInputInvalid` resets the cursor blink (`IsBlinked` goes back to false), so calling it on every message freezes the cursor. Go through `components.InvalidMarks.Sync(key, &ti, invalid)`, from `Update()` only (Rule 110), never from `View()` or a `Cmd`.
355	- **Prefix unchanged.** The focus prefix `●` stays as in Rule 120. The underline adds no cell: the rendered width does not change.
356	- **Fallback.** A terminal without styled underlines gets a plain underline (SGR 4), still readable. Cost: about 60 bytes per underlined character. Risk: SGR 58 and `4:3` on old terminals, to check by hand.
357	
358	```go
359	// ✅ CORRECT — state change only, in Update()
360	f.validation.Revalidate(f.errors())
361	f.marks.Sync(keyName, &f.nameInput, f.validation.Invalid(keyName))
362	
363	// ❌ WRONG — a local underline, and a restyle on every message
364	f.nameInput.SetStyles(lipgloss.NewStyle().Underline(true)...)
365	theme.SetTextInputInvalid(&f.nameInput, true) // in every Update
366	```
367	
368	Forms covered, and where the rules live: `docs/architecture/ui-components.md` ("Invalid form fields"). Out of scope: `templates/form.go`, netdiag, the `ctrl+p` palette, `FilterBar`.
369	
370	Guards: `internal/ui/theme/source_guard_test.go` (`TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo`, `TestGuardInvalidFieldUnderlineHasOneEntryPoint`, `TestGuardDetectors`).

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a Path tab (native path trace, native Linux and WSL2 only: on macOS, Windows and WSL1 `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row prefills it; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target field refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

328:### Rule 130 : a shortcut with nothing to act on is greyed out, not removed
329-
330-**`GetShortcuts()` reflects the current state of the view and of the
331-selected row. What varies is `Disabled`, not whether the entry is present.**
332-
333-#### Mode versus state
334-
335-This is the distinction that decides between the two, and it holds for every
336-view:
337-
338-| | What changes | Why |
339-|---|---|---|
340-| **Mode** — form, confirmation, selection | the **entire list** is replaced | it is not the same vocabulary; greying out `enter → Create` while inside a table would show the union of every mode |
341-| **State** within a mode — selected row, missing tool | the entry **stays**, `Disabled: true` | the column is read out of the corner of the eye, and a list that reorganizes itself under the reader's gaze stops being readable |
342-
343-Two causes of greying out, and only two: the state of the **selected row**,
344-and a **global** unavailability (a tool the machine does not have). An
345-operation in progress is not one of these: it changes on every tick, the row
346-already says so with its activity dot, and a blinking entry says the opposite of
347-what this rule is after.
348-
349-#### Rendering
350-
351-`shortcut.Shortcut.Disabled` is the only mechanism; it is implemented once,
352-in `Shortcuts.ToStrings()`. The key loses its color and its weight
353-(`theme.ShortcutKeyDisabledStyle`, an alias of `ColorDim`), the description
--
450:The header already shows every shortcut via `GetShortcuts()` (Rule 130). Duplicating this information in the viewport creates visual noise, reduces usable space, and lets the two sources drift apart on updates.
451-
452-| Forbidden (in viewport) | Correct (in header) |
453-|--------------------------|----------------------|
454-| `[↑↓/jk] navigate  [c] filter  [esc] close` | `GetShortcuts()` returns `{Key: "↑↓/jk", Description: "Navigate"}`, etc. |
455-| `[↑↓/jk] scroll  [g/G] top/bottom  [enter] new test` | `GetShortcuts()`'s results state returns the scroll shortcuts |
}

input.comment_html:
Revue 470.1 à 470.3 (diff non commité, branche feat/devdesk-470-trace-path-button)

Verdict : approuvé avec réserves, aucun bloquant. Tests netdiag verts, golangci-lint netdiag : 0 issue. Rules 110 (aucune écriture d'état dans View/Cmd), 122, 135, 140 (InvalidMarks.Sync depuis Update, texte repris de parsePathTarget) conformes. Le sous-niveau trace (4) et l'avis Port/DNS (5) sont hors de cette revue.

Important

  • internal/ui/netdiag/header.go:312 — la raison « plateforme non supportée » n'apparaît dans le footer que si le focus est sur Trace Path. Le critère dit « quand le formulaire s'affiche ». Sur macOS, focus sur Target : bouton grisé, footer vide. L'onglet Path l'affiche dans tous les états (path_view.go:109). Correction : retirer la condition focusedField == fieldTraceButton (l'erreur de validation reste prioritaire). À confirmer si l'intention était de ne l'afficher qu'au focus.
  • internal/ui/theme/styles.go:448-452 — bouton disabled : la seule marque du focus est le gras, avec les mêmes couleurs. Dans beaucoup de terminaux le gras ne se voit pas sur texte dim : l'utilisateur ne voit plus où est le curseur (le bouton n'a pas de préfixe ●). Correction : changer aussi le fond au focus (ex. ColorButtonBg avec texte dim) ou ajouter un repère. TestButtonDisabledFocusIsVisible ne prouve que « la chaîne diffère ».

Mineur

  • trace_form_validation_test.go:206-210 — après la correction du lint, var _ = (&Model{}).traceValidation n'asserte plus rien : le test ne vérifie plus les types annoncés par son commentaire. Supprimer le test (le type est déjà imposé par trace_form.go) ou comparer via reflect.
  • trace_form_validation_test.go (TestTraceFormValidationAcceptedRunClearsTheError, fin) — la correction du coder est légitime : en StateRunning le footer porte l'étiquette de progression, « footer vide » était une attente fausse, pas un affaiblissement. Mais la nouvelle assertion est lâche (passe pour n'importe quel texte non-Error). Renforcer : Activity == true ou texte == m.progressLabel().
  • Hors diff, échecs préexistants sous Windows : components/row_status_test.go (séparateurs de chemin) et theme TestFoldHome.

input.message:
Revue DEVDESK-470 (470.1 à 470.3) : verdict approuvé avec réserves, aucun bloquant. Commentaire posté dans Plane (compte reviewer).

Vérifié : `go test ./internal/ui/netdiag` passe, `golangci-lint ./internal/ui/netdiag/...` donne 0 issue. Rules 110, 122, 135 et 140 sont conformes. Pour la 140, `InvalidMarks.Sync` est appelé depuis Update, le statut est dérivé à chaque frame et le texte vient de `parsePathTarget`, donc identique à l'onglet Path. Rule 114 non examinée, comme demandé.

**Bloquants** : aucun.

**Importants**
1. `internal/ui/netdiag/header.go:312` : la raison « plateforme non supportée » n'est affichée dans le footer que si le focus est sur Trace Path.
   - Le critère dit « quand le formulaire s'affiche ». Sur macOS, avec le focus sur Target, le bouton est grisé et le footer est vide.
   - L'onglet Path affiche la raison dans tous les états (`path_view.go:109`).
   - Correction : retirer la condition `m.focusedField == fieldTraceButton`. L'erreur de validation reste prioritaire.
   - À confirmer si l'intention était bien de ne l'afficher qu'au focus.
2. `internal/ui/theme/styles.go:448-452` : sur le bouton disabled, la seule marque du focus est le gras, avec les mêmes couleurs.
   - Le gras est souvent invisible sur du texte dim, et le bouton n'a pas de préfixe ●. L'utilisateur ne voit plus où est le curseur.
   - Correction : changer aussi le fond au focus (par exemple `ColorButtonBg` avec texte dim), ou ajouter un repère.
   - `TestButtonDisabledFocusIsVisible` ne prouve que « la chaîne rendue diffère ».

**Mineurs**
- `trace_form_validation_test.go:206-210` : après la correction du lint, `var _ = (&Model{}).traceValidation` n'asserte plus rien. Le commentaire annonce une vérification de type que le test ne fait plus. Supprimer le test (`trace_form.go` impose déjà le type) ou comparer via reflect.
- `TestTraceFormValidationAcceptedRunClearsTheError`, fin du test : la correction du coder est légitime. En StateRunning le footer porte l'étiquette de progression, donc « footer vide » était une attente fausse. Ce n'est pas un affaiblissement pour coller au code. La nouvelle assertion est cependant lâche : elle passe pour tout texte non-Error. À renforcer avec `Activity == true` ou `text == m.progressLabel()`.
- Hors diff, échecs préexistants sous Windows : `internal/ui/components/row_status_test.go` (séparateurs de chemin) et `theme TestFoldHome`.
- Le lint QF1011 n'apparaît plus : lignes 208-209, le coder a remplacé `var _ components.Validation = …` par `var _ = …`, d'où le premier point mineur ci-dessus.
